conclusions: Three independent controllers sustained three bounded simultaneous 1080p25 captures, each with 750 source buffers, 750 AUs and 750 independently decoded frames. This does not establish production or eight-hour acceptance.

The next five-stream attempt suffered a Type-C controller/Hub remove/add and is not usable for five-stream performance. Retrying with the existing read-only GStreamer registry and staggered startup retained three active 1080p25 streams while the other two failed STREAMON ENOSPC. Two probe conditions changed; the earlier disconnect cause is not established.

On a 2+2+1 controller distribution, all five 720p25 streams started, but one produced 539 source buffers/AUs and timed out at about 12.2fps; another averaged 22.8fps. Independent libavcodec decoded 537/539 AUs on the timed-out stream. The five-stream capture and decode checks failed.

The slow camera remained near 12-13fps in three single-stream mode checks. After swapping it with the blue-port camera, slowness followed the camera, while the other camera delivered about 25fps at the former slow port. Lens illumination/settings/device behavior require investigation; this observation does not prove an exposure cause.

OpenH264 decoded fewer frames than parsed on some otherwise libavcodec-decodable captures. Failed counts and the first local invocation missing isolated library paths are preserved. Client compatibility is unresolved.
count_limit: Individual probe exit codes can indicate a bounded buffer-count path only; they do not certify requested fps, absence of drops, picture quality or whole-system acceptance. Aggregate results retain cadence, EOS, decoded-frame counts and failures.
